analysis:
The PR changes only provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. No production code appears in the supplied diff, so no runtime behavior changes. The patch adds a decodeTable to the StubTokenizer (head lines ~146-155) and a stopStringScope parameter to the makeBridge helper (head ~443, ~462). It adds three tests (head ~847-899): scopedReportNamesTheMatchingCandidate, requestScopeReachesEngineAndReport, and modelScopeIsTheDefault. These tests exercise EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with a ReasoningStopScope, per-request stopStringScope reaching the CBv2Request, and the request scope overriding the model scope. They touch no keys, attestation, encryption, cache storage, authorization or network paths, and add no attack surface. Related threat model areas are T-007/T-056 (output correctness claims) and T-041 (prefix cache). Neither is affected.

The production API the tests call is outside the supplied evidence: submitTokenized's stopStringScope parameter, ReasoningStopScope.scope, and the bridge init's stopStringScope. I can't verify that the production stop-scope logic matches what the tests assert. This is a correctness concern for stop-string handling, not a security regression visible here. One residual question for integration: whether the production request-level stop scope override is derived only from trusted parser or prefix state and never from consumer-controlled input. That would be in production files not supplied in this batch.
